title: Edge Launch Operator Cheatpad (iter 0)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operator-first cheatpad for sellers and SEs running discovery and onboarding conversations for edge/private (VPC/on-prem) pilots. Designed to land the technical conversation in <15m, validate ops constraints, and give a repeatable canary + rollback story for risk-averse infra teams. Draft — very rough.

One-line pitch for operators:
Redwood Private installs into your network and gives a consistent inference runtime with predictable latency and clear operational controls (autoscale, model pinning, KV cache) while leaving control of keys and network traffic in your hands. We prioritize safe fallbacks and integration patterns that avoid production surprises.

3-minute seller script (operator persona):
- Intro (30s): "We specialize in making inference predictable in your environment — low latency, clear resource costs, and enterprise controls. I want to check a few environment details so we can propose a pilot that fits your ops constraints."
- Validation (7x): Ask quick binary checks (listed below).
- Canary promise (45s): "We'll ship a canary plan: deploy small capacity, run synthetic workloads and a traffic mirror for 48–72 hours, and hand over operational dashboards. If SLOs or resource profiles don't match, we rollback or throttle — you keep control."
- Next step (20s): Schedule infra touchpoint + provide deployment checklist and sample Terraform snippet.

Operator validation checklist (fast booleans to confirm in discovery):
- Network: Can you allow outbound to redwood-control.example.com and S3? (Yes/No)
- Ingress/egress: Is egress restricted to specific IPs or via proxy? (proxy/allowlist/block)
- Air-gapped: Is the environment air-gapped? (Yes/No)
- KMS/HSM: Do you have a managed KMS or HSM for customer keys? (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Hashi HSM, none)
- Storage: Is object storage accessible internally? (S3-compatible bucket yes/no)
- Orchestration: Do you use Kubernetes, VMs, or baremetal? (k8s/vm/baremetal)
- GPU access: Are GPUs present and schedulable? (type, driver version)
- Compliance: Any regulatory controls we should know (PCI/PHI/etc)?
- SLAs: Target latency p95 and availability SLOs for pilot?
- Observability: Can we receive Prometheus scraping or push metrics to your telemetry?

Red flags to escalate to solutions engineering (call these out in Slack):
- Full air-gap with zero inbound/outbound allowed and no offline install path defined.
- Strict HSM-only workflow with approvals >3 days for key usage.
- GPU drivers older than supported baseline (list in linked playbook).

Canary plan (template) — high level:
1) Scope: single region/node pool, 1-2 GPUs, canary route limited to internal client(s).
2) Deploy: Provide Helm/Terraform snippet (attach) — start with conservative resources and model quantized variant.
3) Tests: synthetic throughput, latency p50/p95, prefix-cache warmup, KV cache hit rate, end-to-end app latency (app -> rw API -> model).
4) Mirror traffic: optional traffic shadowing at 10–20% of production for 48h.
5) Acceptance: p95 < target, CPU/GPU utilization steady, no memory spikes, error rate < 0.1%.
6) Rollback: scale to zero or disable route; automated rollback runbook included.

Sample canary test snippets (talk track and script):
- "We'll run a 1k-request burst and measure p95; we'll also run a steady-state 10 rps test for 2 hours to observe batching behavior."
- curl-based health check: curl -fsS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://private-api.local/healthz
- Synthetic load: run locust/jmeter config we've provided; point at ingress load balancer only.

Common operator objections and short responses:
- "We don't want any outbound connections." -> "We support an offline install that only needs control-plane artifacts once; we can discuss an airgap kit and host the images on your private registry. SE will own the exact checklist."
- "We need to keep keys in our HSM." -> "Great — we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers. We'll provide a key-split guide and can sign a KMS access attestation for the pilot."
- "What happens if the model spikes cost?" -> "Pilot uses reserved capacity with strict autoscaling profiles and token caps; the canary includes simulated load to validate cost and throttle thresholds."

Pricing hooks for infra leads (concise):
- Pilot pricing: fixed 30-day reserved pilot SKU with soft limits (billing holds, usage alerts).
- Post-pilot: options for reserved capacity commit or pay-as-you-go with cap controls.
- Migration uplift: quantization and batch tuning yields 30–60% cost reduction for common workloads — we include a one-off optimization advisory during pilot.

Slide-by-slide suggested deck (6 slides) — speaker bullets (for SE):
1) Title + 15s: "Why Redwood Private for operators" — emphasize control, visibility, rollback.
2) Problem: "Inference unpredictability: hidden cost, noisy neighbors, unknown latencies" — two quick customer quotes.
3) How we fit: runtime + routing + private control plane (diagram).
4) Canary plan & acceptance criteria (copy of canary above).
5) Risk & rollback (automated throttles, model fallbacks, circuit breakers).
6) Next steps & ask (infra touchpoint, pilot scope doc, legal contacts).

Operational FAQs (quick answers for live calls):
- "How long to deploy?" -> "Typical pilot: 2–5 business days for standard k8s environment; longer if air-gapped or HSM approvals required."
- "Who owns escalation?" -> "Redwood SE + Customer SRE jointly during pilot; escalation matrix in playbook."
- "Can we disable telemetry during pilot?" -> "Yes, only required telemetry for health checks; optional metrics can be restricted."

Open items / TODOs (notes to self):

- Solidify airgap offline installer checklist (Priya).
- Create single-page pilot SOW template and a short legal glossary for procurement (Daniel).
- Run internal dry-run with SRE team and capture timings (Samira).

Quick reference links (for SE on calls):

- Pilot JIRA: JIRA:EDGE-PILOT-242

Notes to self: rough, modular, intended to be pared down into a 1-pager and a 6-slide deck. Keep this doc as living: after each pilot add 1-2 lines of lessons (driver versions, proxy patterns, acceptance thresholds).
